text:
harry: quick flag: zephyr-mini-ptq-v2 canary (streaming + kvcache reuse) shows a bunch of stitched funcall JSONs — looks like objects cut in half then next object starts.

canary-bot: Canary alert: funcall_parse_failure_rate = 9.4% (window 5m) for zephyr-mini-ptq-v2. https://canary.internal/zephyr/ptq/v2

nina: paste one minimal concatenated output when you have it. single example helps a lot.

harry: pasted from raw streams: `{"tool":"update_record","args":{"id":9001,"status":"in_progress"}

{"tool":"emit_event","args":{"topic":"jobs","msg":"ok"}}` — missing close after first object.

olaf: that pattern points to token boundary cutoff. zephyr-mini was PTQ int8 with sequence packing + streaming. Did anyone change EOS handling or the tokenizer special-token merges during quant job?

luca: immediate triage idea: run a small injection test: send deterministic prompts that force the model to emit nested JSON arrays and watch where token ids differ between fp16 and ptq. Collect last 6 token ids for failed sessions.

benchbot: quick sample (300 multi-turn sessions): fp16=parse_failures 0.7%, zephyr-mini-ptq=parse_failures 9.1%, repaired_by_cut=2.8%, unrepaired=6.3%.

qa-bot: Note: some repaired outputs changed top-level "tool" name (2 cases) after cut heuristics. Flagged as repaired_changed_action_count=2.

nina: We need a conservative repair policy: only auto-repair if top-level tool string checksum is preserved after repair. Otherwise mark failed and surface to app.

harry: agreed. Also add repair_confidence and keep raw final token ids in secure S3 for offline tokenizer bisect. Do not store user payloads, only token ids + model meta.

olaf: suggest a 2x2 grid canary: streaming on/off x kvcache reuse on/off, batch sizes 1 and 4. Run 2k sessions, sample token dumps at 1% to start.

luca: will start the grid. I'll implement a parser-rescue that: try strict parse -> if fail, try last '}' cut -> compute action_checksum before/after -> if checksum matches, emit repaired with confidence score proportional to length preserved, else emit failed. Hook behind feature flag.

benchbot: schedule: grid kicking off now. will post aggregate snapshots every 20m.

nina: small safety: never auto-apply repairs for tool names in HIGH_RISK = ["delete_account","revoke_key","transfer_funds"].

harry: action items: @luca implement parser-rescue + feature flag; @nina run grid & collect token-id dumps; @olaf run non-stream mirror baseline for comparison; @benchbot track repaired_changed_action_count.

luca: will push small lib and a telemetry event `funcall.repair.v1` with tags (ok,repaired,failed,repair_confidence,action_checksum_delta).

canary-bot: Update in ~15m or when first 500 sessions complete.

harry: tl;dr: ptq canary shows multi-turn streaming funcall stitching. short-term: conservative repair + telemetry + token-id dumps. medium-term: tokenizer bisect & review quant pipeline if token id drift confirmed.

nina: +1. If bisect shows quant changed token ids for punctuation/whitespace around JSON boundaries, we should block rollout until fixed.

olaf: also consider disabling sequence packing for streaming canaries as a quick mitigation.

harry: thanks all — keep updates concise in this thread.
